issues.body:
## Program

Operator-directed iOS foundation work aligned with AI Core Program #2 and the R1 product boundary.

## User capability

A user can launch a native VisePanda iPhone app and navigate a truthful first-version shell for Today, Ask, Trip, Explore, and Profile.

## Current evidence

VP-V4 is a frontend-only Next.js preview. No native iOS target exists. Auth, live AI, durable Trip APIs, media, and offline persistence are not production-ready.

## Objective

Create the smallest buildable native SwiftUI foundation that establishes navigation, design tokens, localization entry points, accessibility behavior, deterministic preview fixtures, and tests.

## Scope

- Add an isolated ios/VisePanda Xcode project targeting iPhone.
- Use SwiftUI with one NavigationStack per tab.
- Add five stable top-level tabs: Today, Ask, Trip, Explore, Profile.
- Add honest placeholder states and no-live-service disclosure.
- Add zh, en, es, ru, and ar localization resources with RTL support.
- Add unit tests and SwiftUI previews.
- Add an iOS architecture/readme document and synchronized handoff state.

## Anti-goals

- No WebView wrapper.
- No real AI, auth, persistence, inventory, booking, payment, Human Help, SLA, push, media permission, or external API.
- No direct database access or Trip mutation.
- No redesign of the accepted web compatibility layer.
- No App Store submission or signing configuration.

## Interface impact

No production backend contract. The iOS app consumes deterministic local placeholder content only. Future API consumers must use versioned server contracts after R1/R2 gates.

## Dependencies

Operator instruction in the current Codex session. Future runtime integration remains blocked by R1 Gate #17 and authenticated session/product shell contracts.

## Acceptance

- Xcode project builds for an iPhone Simulator.
- Swift tests cover stable tab identity and placeholder capability status.
- Five tabs preserve independent NavigationStack ownership.
- Dynamic Type, VoiceOver labels, Reduce Motion, Reduce Transparency, light/dark appearance, and Arabic RTL have explicit support or fixtures.
- UI makes unavailable capabilities explicit.
- Existing pnpm checks remain unchanged and any unrun checks are disclosed.

## Allowed paths

- ios/**
- docs/adr/**
- docs/agents/issue-execution-contract.md
- docs/handoff.json
- generated HANDOFF.md and CONTEXT.md only through repository scripts
- README.md only if required to link the iOS project

## Forbidden paths

- app/**
- components/**
- lib/**
- public/**
- existing Web UI styling and assets
- database, provider, auth, payment, or deployment configuration

## Risk

Primary risk is building UI against unstable runtime contracts. Mitigation: no network integration, local fixtures only, and explicit maturity labels.

## Rollback

Remove the IOS-01 additions under ios/ and its registered documentation/contract entries. No data migration or external account rollback exists.

## Documentation impact

Add an accepted iOS foundation ADR and ios/README.md. Update handoff/index artifacts through deterministic scripts.

## Observation

Owner: operator/product. Cadence: review at R1 Gate #17 and again when R2 auth/session contracts freeze. Measure: simulator build stays green and the first real vertical slice requires no navigation or ownership rewrite.
